The Islamist militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack in central Mogadishu, group spokesman Abu Musab said. The attack started when two suicide bombers blew up their car at the entrance of the two-story building that houses the Ministry of Education, Culture and Higher Education, Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said. Five gunmen then entered the building and shot people inside, Yusuf said.

One war was enough for 87-year-old Gregory Margolin. When he was 16, he fought in the Soviet Red Army during World War II. He fought against the Nazis, while his family fled. “I did not show that I was Jewish,” Margolin says. “But it did not matter because people were being killed left and right. All around me.” This year, in Ukraine, he found himself again surrounded by war. Margolin was a sniper and became a commander in the army. His old uniform still has medals from his time in the military. His granddaughter Liora still marvels at his stories from the war. She is amazed that he managed to survive.
